newsitem.title: USA: Kemp blasts Republicans for backing off tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Kemp blasts Republicans for backing off tax cuts.

text.p: Defeated Republican vice presidential candidate Jack Kemp Thursday blasted Republican leaders for retreating on their promise to cut taxes, saying the move had eroded confidence in the stock market.

In a hard-hitting letter to House Speaker Newt Gingrich and other top Republican House leaders, Kemp said a complete overhaul of the tax code and elimination of the Internal Revenue Service in its current form should be the top priority for the party.
"If Republicans cannot reach agreement on this fundamental priority, we should break up the party and start over," Kemp wrote in the letter, a copy of which was made available to Reuters.
Gingrich angered conservatives this week by proposing that Republicans put off a major tax cut to help achieve a balanced budget deal with President Clinton.
"We don't want to get into a trap where every time we propose any kind of healthy change in the government, liberals have automatic screaming about tax cuts," Gingrich said.
"So let's take tax cuts away for a moment. Let's just talk about balancing the budget. Now what's the liberal excuse for not balancing the budget?"

Clinton welcomed the statement and invited the heads of the House and Senate budget committees to the White House Wednesday to begin negotiations on a balanced budget. The sides agreed to a three-week effort to reach agreement.
But Kemp, who is already beginning to organise a presidential bid for the year 2000, said Republicans had become confused about their aims.
"We have allowed balancing the budget to assume the status of a 'moral crusade.' With all due respect, it is not," he wrote.
"The moral imperative is to reestablish limited government and to maximize freedom for the American people."
Kemp said Gingrich's statement had "stopped the stock market in its tracks ... indicating to me that investors are losing faith that they will see capital gains tax rate reductions this year."
Kemp urged Republicans to cut capitals gains and estate taxes this year while negotiating the best deal they could get with Clinton. He said failure to do so might be fatal to Republicans.
